gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-alan-sans: Cherry Swash draws a wide, horseshoe-shaped c and flat, contrast-free letters with real swagger, while Alan Sans holds its curve tails back. Its sans-serif lines read lightly.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-albert-sans: Albert Sans keeps its apertures open even at tiny sizes, and its strokes never change thickness with direction. Cherry Swash then sits above it, loud and wide-mouthed, giving the page a confident front door.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-alef: Cherry Swash flows like one smooth drawn wire, heavy and sure of itself. Alef follows in sans-serif, its open-ended curves running clean, so you can size it up a touch without losing that lightness.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Chunky, wide-grinning and flat-lined, Cherry Swash has plain constant-width strokes, while Alegreya Sans SC keeps a welcoming gap in its c. One shouts; the other talks.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-almarai: A horseshoe-wide c and diagonals as heavy as the verticals make Cherry Swash instantly recognizable, and Almarai follows in sans-serif with lines that never pinch shut or swell, so paragraphs glide.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-amarna: Loud, wide and unmistakably friendly. Cherry Swash takes the spotlight, and Amarna backs it with plain sans strokes that stay uniform and uncluttered in every tiny counter.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-andika: Andika reads with generous, easy-turning s shapes and tails as thick as its stems, nothing fussy anywhere. Cherry Swash and Andika both love sturdy strokes, and that shared heft is what ties them together.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-antic: Big-hearted and bold up top, Cherry Swash opens its c like a horseshoe, while Antic below looks drawn with one nib. Its sans-serif mouths stay unjoined, like chalk arcs, so lines flow gently.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-ar-one-sans: Curves as heavy as the stems make Cherry Swash look like knotted cord. AR One Sans lifts its brush ends away before each curve closes, so a long read feels light and breezy.
